body_md_excerpt:
7 verifiers of open math problems curated by Alejandro Zarzuelo Urdiales for the Open Math Challange.

## Start here

1. [Register for the event](https://luma.com/yzp9abvr), using the registration link on [OpenMath](https://rsihouse.ai/openmath). Coordinate your team of 1–4 with the organizers.
2. Sign in to AutoLab, choose a runnable hill below, and read its README, scoring direction, and version.
3. Click **Start a climb**. For results tracked on AutoLab, choose **On AutoLab**, select AutoLab's agent or your coding agent, set a model budget, and connect or rent compute before starting. Compute is billed separately.
4. Inspect experiments in your climb and compare scored runs through the hill's **Leaderboard**. Follow the organizers' separate submission and review instructions for competition credit.

A **list** curates problems. A **hill** fixes the task and evaluator. A **climb** records your team's attempt and experiments. A hill score measures its stated task; mathematical acceptance also requires the competition's formal artifact/certificate and review.

## Seven runnable hills

Six of these are the problems presented in the organizer deck (the Ramsey multiplicity hill replaces the saturated linear-arboricity catalog in that selection). The seventh, Erdős Problem #3, was added afterward and carries an external cash prize.

### Kobon triangles

Arrange straight lines and maximize the exact count of bounded triangular faces.

[[alejandrozu/kobon-triangles]]

### Clique clusters and K4 Ramsey multiplicity

Search weighted clique-block templates whose infinite blow-up families improve a published upper bound.

[[alejandrozu/clique-cluster-ramsey-multiplicity]]

### 3 by 3 matrix multiplication

Search exact bilinear decompositions of the 3 by 3 matrix-multiplication tensor.

[[alejandrozu/matrix-multiplication-tensor-3x3]]

### Grothendieck constant witnesses

Construct exact matrix and vector certificates that improve a lower bound for the Grothendieck constant.

[[alejandrozu/grothendieck-constant-witnesses]]

### Collatz modular descent

Certify descent on residue classes using exact arithmetic; finite coverage does not settle Collatz.

[[alejandrozu/collatz-modular-descent]]

### Busy Beaver 6 certificates

Construct six-state Turing machines with long, exactly replayable halting runs; these certify lower bounds.

[[alejandrozu/busy-beaver-6-certificates]]

### Erdős Problem #3 (arithmetic progressions in dense-sum sets) — $5,000 prize

If $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $\sum_{n\in A} 1/n = \infty$, must $A$ contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions? The $k=3$ case is known (Bloom–Sisask); $k\geq 4$ is open. Erdős offered \$5,000 for a proof or disproof, and the prize is administered through the [Erdős Problems](https://www.erdosproblems.com/3) site, independently of this competition. A hill score measures the hill's stated task only; the prize and mathematical acceptance follow that site's and the organizers' own review.

[[ottogin/erdos-3]]
